query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A minor microalloying addition of niobium (Nb) to (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 will induce the in‐situ formation of fine, ductile Nb-rich precipitates at grain boundaries that enhance the alloy’s mechanical integrity (i.e., increased compressive strength and reduced cracking) without substantially impairing its large caloric response under applied field and pressure operations.
generation.material_initial_state: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy exhibiting a large caloric response but with poor structural integrity and a tendency to crack.
generation.intervention: Incorporate a small amount (≈1–2 at.%) of Nb into the alloy composition during synthesis.
generation.conditions: Under the same applied magnetic field and pressure-field conditions (and temperature range) used for caloric performance measurements; mechanical tests (compression and crack propagation) should be performed at both room temperature and within the operating thermal range of the caloric effect.
generation.structural_mediator: The Nb addition is expected to promote the formation of nanoscale, uniformly distributed Nb-rich precipitates (secondary phase) primarily at grain boundaries, leading to enhanced intergranular cohesion.
generation.mechanism: The introduced Nb will provide solid-solution strengthening and trigger an in-situ precipitation of a ductile second phase, which blunts crack initiation and propagation. This microstructural alteration improves overall mechanical robustness while leaving the magnetostructural transformation (which drives the caloric response) largely unaffected.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in compressive strength (e.g., from the low tens of MPa in composite routes to values on the order of 150 MPa or higher) and reduced crack formation, while the magnitude and sensitivity of the caloric response (magneto- and pressure-induced) remain within approximately 10% of the baseline performance of the undoped alloy.
generation.baseline: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 without Nb, which shows high caloric performance but poor mechanical integrity with cracking under operational loads.
generation.boundary: Valid under applied-field, pressure-field, and temperature regimes typically used to induce the caloric response; experiments are limited to the rare-earth-free composition domain and similar processing conditions.
generation.uncertainty: While the strength improvement mechanism is supported by similar strategies in high-entropy systems, the precise impact on the caloric response remains uncertain. There may be a trade-off if Nb addition subtly shifts transformation temperatures or kinetics, but the hypothesis expects any such changes to be minor (<10%).

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two sets of samples: one set of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 and a second set with 1–2 at.% Nb added using identical processing routes. Subject both sets to identical applied-field and pressure-field cyclic tests. Measure mechanical properties (compressive strength, crack initiation and propagation under loading) and caloric performance (magnitude of caloric effect, transformation temperatures, and response rates).
measurements: Compressive strength (MPa) and strain to failure
Crack density and propagation characteristics via microscopy
Magnetocaloric/pressure-induced caloric effect magnitude and transformation temperature shifts
Thermal conductivity, if relevant to performance
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Nb-doped alloy does not exhibit a statistically significant improvement in mechanical integrity (e.g., compressive strength increase beyond baseline by ~50% or more and reduced cracking) OR if the caloric response decreases by more than approximately 10% relative to the undoped alloy, then the hypothesis is falsified.
